labelChirho: Qal: be pleased with, delight in
descriptionChirho: To take pleasure in, be favorable toward, or have goodwill toward a person or situation; the core Qal sense expressing emotional disposition of approval or delight, confirmed by Korean 기뻐하다 and Swahili -pendezwa (be pleased) as distinct from active acceptance of offerings.

To receive or accept favorably, especially offerings, sacrifices, or persons presented before God; distinguished from the 'be pleased' sense by the transitive act of reception, confirmed by Korean 받다/받아들이다 (receive/accept), Swahili -kubali (accept), and Arabic أَقْبَلُ (accept).

A specialized sense used of the land 'enjoying' or 'paying off' its missed sabbath years during the exile (Lev 26:34-43, 2 Chr 36:21); the Hifil causative form appears alongside Qal in this usage, with Spanish pagará (will pay) and disfrutó (enjoyed) confirming the distinct semantic field.

The Qal passive participle functioning adjectivally to describe someone or something as favored, acceptable, or well-regarded; Arabic مَرْضِيًّا / مَقْبُولًا (accepted/approved) and Korean 은혜를 받는 (receiving grace) confirm the stative adjectival sense.

The Nifal passive stem expressing the state or event of being accepted or found acceptable, typically of sacrificial offerings; Korean 받아들여지리라 (will be accepted) and Swahili -kubaliwa (be accepted) consistently use passive voice, and Arabic يُقْبَلُ (passive of accept) confirms the stem distinction.

The Piel intensive stem meaning to seek to please, curry favor, or entreat someone for goodwill; Arabic يَسْتَرْضُونَ (seek satisfaction from) uses the Form X (istafʿala) pattern indicating seeking, and Swahili watatafuta huruma kwa (they will seek mercy from) confirms the factitive/seeking nuance.

The Hitpael reflexive stem meaning to reconcile oneself, make oneself acceptable, or seek to restore favor; Arabic يَستَرضي (seek to please/reconcile) and Swahili atapatanisha (he will reconcile) confirm the reflexive-reciprocal meaning distinct from the simple Qal.
